_README: Standing figures marked by hand, for the equal-height horizon construction.
Click a head then that figure's foot in the review app (section 1b); it writes here.
Coordinates are normalised: x fraction of plate width, y fraction of height,
origin top-left. tools/equal_height_horizon.py turns two or more figures into a
horizon with NO assumption about how tall anyone is, and reports the residual.
verified:false means the points were placed by eye and not checked against a
grid. Nothing unverified is written into data/perspective.overrides.json unless
someone asks for it explicitly, because a mark is an observation and an override
is a claim. The emblem-42 entry below is a worked EXAMPLE of the format, not a
measurement: its own readout says the horizon cuts both figures at 0.459 of
their height, which is too low for eye level and means the points need redoing.
